Galway and Roscommon Education and Training
 Board
 Service Plan
 2025

Foreword from Chief Executive
I am pleased to present the Annual Service Plan for 2025 on behalf of Galway and Roscommon
Education and Training Board (GRETB). This plan outlines our commitment to delivering high-quality
education and training services, supporting learners, and contributing to the social and economic
development of our communities. This provision will be in accordance with the resources allocated
by the Department of Education and Youth, the Department of Further and Higher Education,
Research, innovation and Science, the Department of Children, Disability and Equality and other
funding bodies.

 As we embark on this year’s journey, we remain dedicated to our core mission of providing
accessible, inclusive, and innovative learning opportunities for all. Over the past eleven years, GRETB
has demonstrated the resilience and adaptability of our staff, learners, and stakeholders. Building on
this foundation, we aim to enhance our services, foster excellence in teaching and learning, and
further strengthen our partnerships with key stakeholders, including government agencies,
employers, and community organizations.

 This Annual Service Plan aligns with national and regional policies, ensuring that our objectives
contribute to the broader goals of the education and training sector. Key priorities for this year
include expanding access to further education and training (FET), advancing digital transformation in
learning, promoting lifelong learning, and addressing skills gaps to meet evolving societal and
workforce needs.

 Our continued investment in staff development, infrastructure, and learner supports will be
instrumental in achieving these priorities. We remain committed to ensuring that our services are
learner-centered, equitable, and responsive to the changing needs of society.

I would like to extend my gratitude to our staff, learners, and partners for their ongoing dedication
and collaboration. Together, we will continue to build an education and training system that
empowers individuals and strengthens communities.

I look forward to the successful implementation of this plan and the positive impact it will have on
all those we serve.




David Leahy
Chief Executive
Galway & Roscommon Education and Training Board
31st January 2025




2|Page

1. Background Information
GRETB provide a wide range of education services across a very large region in the West of Ireland,
catering for a diverse population with different educational, social and cultural needs. These services
include, community national schools, post-primary schools, further education and training, and
community-based education programmes and training, and the Outdoor Education Centre in
Petersburg. GRETB also runs and manages an Education Service in Castlerea Prison and an Education
Centre for refugees in Ballaghaderreen. GRETB is the lead partner for three Music Generation
projects (County Galway, Galway City and Roscommon). In accordance with the Education and
Training Boards Act 2013, it is also responsible for supporting the provision, coordination,
administration and assessment of youth work services in counties Galway and Roscommon.

Galway and Roscommon Education and Training Board (GRETB) has a corporate structure which is
made up of a democratically appointed committee (reserve) and a management team (executive).

GRETB is the second largest ETB in the country, in terms of geographical area, and includes three
islands. County Galway has the single largest and most populous Gaeltacht area in the country.
Promoting Gaeilge is an essential element of GRETB’s core service, as noted in objective 4.1 of our
Strategy Statement. We have eight Coláistί Lán-Ghaeilge and a number of our Further Education and
Training centres in Connemara, operate through Irish.

2. Vision, Mission and Core Values
GRETB Strategy Statement 2022-2026 was approved by our Board in December 2021. In preparing
this Strategy Statement, key national strategies, such as the DoE’s Strategy, the FET Strategy, and the
other national strategies were considered. Common themes were identified, and these formed the
basis for the development of GRETB’s strategy. A collaborative cross-sectoral consultation process
took place with key stakeholders. Arising from this, strategic goals and objectives were identified,
and a five-year implementation plan has been developed. Progress on the actions will be monitored
by the Senior Management Team.

Strategic Goals
GRETB’s Strategy Statement sets out four high level strategic goals, which are in line with national strategies
on education:


 PEOPLE - To value, develop and support our staff,
 students and learners


 PROGRAMMES - To provide high quality, responsive
 and inclusive education and training programmes


 PROCESS - To lead in organisation development and
 corporate governance


 POTENTIAL - To raise the profile of GRETB and enhance
 provision in partnership with our key stakeholders




Each goal has its own set of strategic objectives which will be met through a series of supporting actions. These
goals and objectives have been designed to assist GRETB to avail of opportunities which may arise, and to
meet the challenges the organisation will face over the next five years.

3. 1 Statement of Service – Schools
GRETB is patron to 19 post-primary schools and 2 Community National Schools (CNS). As patron, GRETB
provides a range of supports and services to each school including, IT, programme development, HR,
governance, financial, capital, quality assurance, policy development, enhancing teaching and learning for the
2024-2025 academic year, and child protection oversight.

Over the past ten years, GRETB has seen continuous growth in school enrolment, reflecting the trust and
confidence that families place in their schools. This growth is expected to continue, providing even more
opportunities for students.

GRETB’s Community Colleges are an integral part of their local communities. They are inclusive and facilitate
young people in meeting their full potential in society through the provision of high standards in education
and informed citizenship within empowering, supportive and progressive schools.

Programmes being offered in our Community Colleges include Junior Certificate, Junior Certificate Schools
Programme (JCSP), Transition Year, Leaving Certificate Established, Leaving Certificate Applied Programme
(LCAP), Leaving Certificate Vocational Programme (LCVP), Post Leaving Certificate courses (PLC), Music School,
Scéim Bhliain ar Oileán (One academic year offshore island), Adult Education and evening classes
A full range of subjects including languages, the humanities, arts, technology and science are offered at both
junior and senior cycle. Five GRETB post-primary schools have been selected to offer the new Leaving Cert
subject of Drama, Film, and Theatre Studies (DFTS) in 2025.

During 2025 GRETB schools will continue their participation in an extensive range of cocurricular and
extracurricular competitions and events e.g. TY trips, ERASMUS, school musicals, Young Scientists, music,
sports, literary, arts and work experience.

In order to ensure the highest quality of teaching and learning and the best possible educational experience
for our students, supports will be offered by GRETB to all schools in:

 • Special Education and Learning Support;
 • CPD for teachers and support staff, Numeracy and Literacy, Technology Enhanced Teaching and
 Learning;
 • CPD Child Protection (on school request for existing teachers and as an integral part of GRETB new
 staff induction programme);
 • Oideachas trí mheán na Gaeilge chomh maith le hoideachas Gaeltachta, 8 GRETB schools provide Irish-
 Medium Education;
 • Development programmes for GRETB’s Principals, Deputy Principals and Middle Management post
 holders in conjunction with OIDE, Teaching Council and other relevant agencies;
 • Other key staff cohorts, including SNAs, administration and caretaking staff

In addition to the above, support will also be offered in the areas of policy making and governance through
ongoing work and training with schools and Boards of Managements (BOM). In 2024, new Boards of
Management were appointed in most of GRETB schools and training was facilitated.

GRETB engages directly with ETBI and other national bodies and education partners to develop Education
Policy and to assist GRETB Schools in having their input included within education policy and education
practice decision and discussion forums.

GRETB appointed a Regional Education and Language Team (REALT) Coordinator in 2022, whose primary role
is to assist Ukrainian and International Protection children in securing school places in the region. In 2025 the


6|Page

Co-ordinator will continue to support schools to meet the educational needs of these children as they emerge,
and to advise and support the Department in developing new capacity where required.

The school Ethos Co-ordinator will continue to embed the five core values of care, community, equality,
respect and excellence in education into all GRETB post primary and community national schools in 2025. This
is done through the Professional Learning Network (PLN) of Ethos Team Leads, in conjunction with Ethos
teams in schools. All new Boards of Management are receiving ETHOS training, and Principals and Deputy
Principals have engaged with the ETB ethos roadshow.

A GRETB SSE Co-ordinator was appointed in 2022 to develop the process of School Self Evaluation (SSE) as a
tool for reflection and improvement relating to the “Looking at our School” (LAOS) framework, with a focus
on professional collaboration and leadership development. The SSE Co-ordinator and the Director of Schools
are collaborating to offer an Aspiring Leaders professional learning opportunity for a cohort of teachers for
the 2024-2025 school year. This initiative aims to cultivate leadership skills and foster professional growth
among educators, preparing them for future leadership roles within GRETB.

To support the leadership development, GRETB has a principal representative on the ETB Principals Network
and the Líonra Gaeloideachais.




GRETB works with universities from which participants in Professional Masters in Education (PMEs)
programmes undertake teaching placements in GRETB schools and has formalised an agreement with regard
to Garda Vetting and Child Protection.

All GRETB post-primary schools are involved in provision mapping. Provision Mapping is a process that allows
schools to identify, list and evaluate the evidence-informed provisions and supports in place for students across
the Continuum of Support in one summary document. Provision Mapping (PM) provides a framework to
develop shared commitment to inclusive education between school staff, students and parents. Research has
shown that holding collective responsibilities for all students in a school community contributes to a better
school experience for students with additional needs and disabilities. Provision Mapping also builds leadership
capacity within GRETB to respond to our increasingly diverse student populations. Provision Mapping is
supported by our inclusion coordinator and the SENCO Community of Practice that is constantly evolving.

In 2024, Communities of Practice have been established in the areas of Additional Educational Needs (AEN),
Delivering Equality of Opportunity in Schools (DEIS), Guidance, and Teaching and Learning. These communities

7|Page

provide valuable opportunities for teachers to meet, collaborate, and engage in meaningful discussions,
fostering professional growth and enhancing educational practices. This initiative will adopt a sustained
approach, ensuring ongoing support and development for teachers.


GRETB has 19 post primary schools and 2 CNS, 8 of these schools deliver education through the medium of
Irish, including 7 Gaeltacht colleges. GRETB is distinguished as the only Education and Training Board (ETB) in
Ireland with three post-primary schools situated on isolated offshore islands. Furthermore, it has the highest
number of Gaeltacht and Gaelcholáistí schools, as well as the largest student population learning through the
medium of Irish, compared to any other ETB in the country.

4.2 Statement of Service – Further Education and Training (FET)

GRETB’s FET provision from levels 1 to 6 is delivered with the intention of offering wider opportunities to our
learners to grow personally and professionally; to increase knowledge, skills and confidence; and to progress
through the FET system to higher education and employment. Our Community Education, Community
Training, ABE, Youthreach, VTOS, BTEI, Training/Traineeship, Apprenticeship and PLC provision will continue
to offer programmes, courses, and interventions that are attractive, relevant, and offer possibilities to
progress. GRETB will continue to simplify the access and journey into, though, and out of its FET provision,
for existing and potential learners through full and part-time offerings as it evolves towards a ‘FET College of
the Future’ model.

The FET Department will continue to enhance access and transition pathways to learners, increase
engagement and participation with local industry and employers, increase GRETB’s presence across all fora
including media, traditional and social, and provide strong supports to staff and learners in the maintaining of
high standards of teaching, learning and assessment using the latest methodologies and technologies.
Working in tandem with Training and PLC provision are the following units - Provision & Pathways; Inclusion;
Support and Development; Enterprise and Strategy.




The FET department is committed to implementing GRETB’s Strategy Statement 2022-2026 and its associated
actions. In this context, the key initiatives and developments for 2025 are set as follows:

Engage with our funders SOLAS in continued planning for the College of the Future as announced for GRETB
by Minister Simon Harris in November 2022. A Preliminary Business Case was developed throughout 2023 and
submitted in January 2024. A second Preliminary Business Case was submitted in January 2025. GRETB senior

4.3 Statement of Service – Organisational Support and Development
Central to the delivery of GRETB’s services is the Organisation Support and Development (OSD) pillar which
plays a critical role in supporting schools and centres. The OSD team’s goals are to enhance the processes and
procedures that underpin good corporate governance in GRETB, and to ensure that the human, financial and
infrastructural resources are deployed efficiently and effectively across our schools, centres and other
services. GRETB has an estimated budget of €153m for 2025, approximately 2000 staff and over 27,000
learners/beneficiaries.

OSD is comprised of six functional area, Finance, Buildings, Procurement, Corporate Services, HR and IT.
These areas provide a range of services to support schools and centres (see details below).

FINANCE

 • Budget and financial reporting
 • Treasury - banking, receipts and reconciliations
 • Preparation of Annual Financial Statements
 • Processing of travel and subsistence claims
 • Learner and apprentices' payments
 • Creditors
 • Co-ordination of audits from C&AG, IAU and ESF Audits, and implementation of recommendations
 • Oversight for financial compliance, and reporting to the Finance Committee and ARC
 • Asset Management in conjunction with IT
 • Engagement with ESBS on shared services projects



BUILDINGS

 • Managing large capital projects - new schools/centres, extensions, refurbishment, and temporary
 accommodation
 • Summer Works Projects
 • Emergency Works Scheme
 • Assistance on non-ETB schools' capital projects when requested by the Department
 • Climate Action Projects, Audits and Reports
 • Health and Safety at Work
 • Providing advice and guidance on all building, climate and H&S queries
 • Representing GRETB on external Building related bodies and forums
